stem: What is the expression for mass per unit length (λ) of a uniform rod of mass M and length L? (a) λ = M×L (b) λ = L/M (c) λ = M/L (d) λ = 1/(ML)
A rod has mass 10 kg and length 4 m. What is its mass per unit length? (a) 0.4 kg/m (b) 2.5 kg/m (c) 4 kg/m (d) 10 kg/m
A uniform rod of mass 12 kg and length 6 m lies on the x-axis. What is the mass of a 2 m segment? (a) 2 kg (b) 3 kg (c) 4 kg (d) 5 kg
A uniform thin rod of length 1.2 m is bent at its midpoint to form a right angle (90°). Find the distance of the centre of mass from the bending point.

Four point masses P, Q, R and S with respective masses 1 kg, 1 kg, 2 kg and 2 kg form the corners of a square of side a, taken in order P, Q, R, S around the square. The centre of mass of the system will be farthest from (a) P only (b) R and S (c) R only (d) P and Q
A uniform square plate abcd has a mass of 1 kg. If two point masses each of 20 g are placed at the corners b and c as shown, then the centre of mass shifts on the line (a) OW (b) OX (c) OY (d) OZ
Locate the centre of mass of arrangement shown in figure. The three rods are identical in mass and length. (a) (L/2, L/2) (b) (L/3, 0) (c) (L/3, L/2) (d) (0, L/3)

answer: b At the midpoint of the rod
stem: The centre of mass of a uniform rod lies: (a) At one end of the rod (b) At the midpoint of the rod (c) At one-fourth of its length from one end (d) Outside the rod
book_key: b At the midpoint of the rod

stem: Three identical spheres, each of mass 1 kg are kept as shown in figure, touching each other, with their centres on a straight line. If their centres are marked P, Q, R respectively, the distance of centre of mass of the system from P is (a) (PQ + PR + QR)/3 (b) (PQ + PR)/3 (c) (PQ + QR)/3 (d) (PR + QR)/3

Mass is distributed uniformly over a thin square plate. If two end points of a diagonal are (−2, 0) and (2, 2), what are the co-ordinates of the centre of mass of plate? (a) (2, 1) (b) (2, 2) (c) (1, 0) (d) (0, 1)

Mass is distributed uniformly over a thin triangular plate and positions of two vertices are given by (1, 3) and (2, −4). What is the position of 3rd vertex if centre of mass of the plate lies at the origin? (a) (1, −2) (b) (−2, 4) (c) (−3, 1) (d) (1, 2)
A uniform wire of length L is bent in the form of a circle. The shift in its centre of mass, keeping its midpoint fixed, is Lx/(4π), find x ?

Figure shows a composite system of two uniform rods of the same material and cross-section (same mass per unit length): a rod of length 2L along the y-axis from O and a rod of length L along the x-axis from O. Then the coordinates of the centre of mass of the system of rods are (a) (L/2, 2L/3) (b) (L/4, 2L/3) (c) (L/6, 2L/3) (d) (L/6, L/3)
A rod of length 3 m has its mass per unit length directly proportional to distance x from one of its ends. Then its centre of gravity from that end will be at (a) 1.5 m (b) 2 m (c) 2.5 m (d) 3.0 m

The mass of a uniform ladder of length 5 m is 20 kg. A person of mass 60 kg stands on the ladder at a distance of 2 m (measured along the ladder) from the bottom. Find the position (in m) of the centre of mass of the ladder and man from the bottom, measured along the ladder. (Ignore height of man)

One end of a thin uniform rod of length L and mass M 1 is rivetted to the centre of a uniform circular disc of radius ‘r’ and mass M 2 so that both are coplanar. The centre of mass of the combination from the centre of the disc is LM 1 / (x(M 1 + M 2 )), find x?
A uniform rod of length 1 m is bent at its midpoint to make 90° angle. The distance of the centre of mass from the centre of the rod is (a) 36.1 cm (b) 25.2 cm (c) 17.7 cm (d) Zero
Find centre of mass distance from point O of the uniform circular arc shown in figure. (The arc has radius R and subtends a total angle φ at its centre O.)

The linear mass density (λ) of a rod of length l kept along x-axis varies as λ = α + βx, where α and β are positive constants. The centre of mass of the rod is at (a) (2β + 3αL)L / (2(2β + αL)) (b) (3α + 2βL)L / (3(2α + βL)) (c) (3β + 2αL)L / (3(2β + αL)) (d) (3β + 2αL)L / (3β + 2α)

Given: A U-shaped uniform wire of sides 2 l , l and l . The x and y co-ordinates of the centre of mass of each side are shown in Fig. [vertical side of length 2 l at (0, l ); upper arm of length l at ( l /2, 2 l ); lower arm of length l at ( l /2, 0)]. The x and y co-ordinates of the centre of mass of wire is ( l /4x, l x), find x?

Three bricks each of length L and mass M are arranged as shown from the wall. [The bottom brick touches the wall; the middle brick overhangs it by L/2 and the top brick overhangs the middle one by L/4.] The distance of the centre of mass of the system from the wall is (a) L/4 (b) L/2 (c) (3/2) L (d) (11/12) L

Locate the centre of mass of a uniform thick hemispherical bowl (solid of uniform density) with inner and outer radii a and 2a. Given that the COM of a solid hemisphere of radius R lies at 3R/8 from its centre, the COM of the bowl is at x·a from the common centre; find x.

A thin uniform wire is bent to form the two equal sides AB and AC of triangle ABC, where AB = AC = 5 cm. The third side BC of length 6 cm is made from uniform wire of twice the density (mass per unit length) of the first. The distance of centre of mass from A is (a) 34/11 cm (b) 11/34 cm (c) 34/9 cm (d) 11/45 cm

Five uniform circular plates, each of diameter b and mass m are laid out in a pattern shown. Using the origin shown, find the y-coordinate of the centre of mass of the five-plate system. (a) b/5 (b) b/3 (c) 4b/5 (d) 2b/5

Seven particles, each of mass m are placed at the seven corners of a cube of side a but one corner is vacant, as shown in figure. The coordinates of the centre of mass of the system is (a) (2a/7, 2a/7, 2a/7) (b) (3a/7, 3a/7, 3a/7) (c) (a/3, a/3, a/3) (d) (5a/11, 5a/11, 5a/11)

A uniform wire is bent into the structure shown in the figure and placed on a table. It consists of two half rings of radius R and two straight parts of length πR; each half ring stands in a vertical plane with its diameter on the table, and both straight parts lie on the table. The height of the COM from the table is (a) 2R/π (b) R/π (c) R/2 (d) zero

Look at the drawing given in the figure which has been drawn with ink of uniform line-thickness. The mass of ink used to draw each of the two inner circles, and each of the two line segments is m. The mass of the ink used to draw the outer circle is 6m. The coordinates of the centres of the different parts are : outer circle (0, 0), left inner circle (−a, a), right inner circle (a, a), vertical line (0, 0) and horizontal line (0, −a). The y-coordinate of the centre of mass of the ink in this drawing is (a) a/10 (b) a/8 (c) a/12 (d) a/3

A thin uniform semi-circular plate and a semi-circular ring of same mass and radius R are joined as shown (plate forms the lower half, ring the upper half, the X-axis touching the plate at O). The y-coordinate of the centre of mass of the system w.r.t. the shown coordinate system is (a) R(1 + 1/(3π)) (b) R(1 − 1/(3π)) (c) R(π + 1/(3π)) (d) R

A piece of uniform paper (figure 1) is in the form of a square of side 2a. Its two right-hand corners are folded to make it appear like figure 2, both corners being put together at the centre O of the square. If O is taken to be (0, 0) with the x-axis pointing right, the centre of mass of the new system will be at (a) (−a/8, 0) (b) (−a/6, 0) (c) (a/12, 0) (d) (−a/12, 0)

A uniform solid right circular cone of base radius R is joined to a uniform solid hemisphere of radius R and of the same density, as shown. The centre of mass of the composite solid lies at the centre of base of the cone. The height of the cone is (a) 1.5R (b) √3R (c) 3R (d) 2√3R

A thin uniform sheet of metal of uniform thickness is cut into the shape bounded by the line x = a and the curves y = ±kx², as shown. The centre of mass lies on the x-axis; find its x-coordinate. (a) (2/3)a (b) (3/4)a (c) (4/5)a (d) (5/6)a
